subject: MSA: Opt-out safeguard proposal and notice window alternatives
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: MSA: Opt-out safeguard proposal and notice window alternatives

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a redline that attempts to bridge two sticking points: auto-renew notice timing and a narrow termination-for-convenience (TFC) path that both sides can accept. High level proposal:

- Auto-renew: keep standard one-year term with automatic annual renewal, but add a structured opt-out signaling process (two reminders at 90/60 days + a formal notice window of 30 days to opt out). This reduces surprise churn and gives both sides a predictable timeline.
- Notice window alternatives: offer Company the option to elect a shorter 45-day notice for pilot or limited accounts by checking an Order Form box; otherwise the default remains 60 days.
- Termination for convenience: mutual TFC allowed, but include an operational transition package: customer can opt for either 30-days limited support (no fee) or a paid 90-day transition at a pro-rata rate; also include a cap to prevent abuse (one unilateral TFC per 24 months).

If that framing sounds ok we can present a single-sheet summary to procurement and legal at Orbyx. Attached: \"MSA_optout_safeguard_redline_v1.pdf\" and a draft Order Form amendment we can use to flag the 45-day pilot option.

Ask: please confirm whether your procurement team needs a formal procurement questionnaire before we circulate the redline to legal. Also let me know whether Orbyx will accept a one-time transitional support fee if you select the paid 90-day option.

Goal: get to a legal redline cycle this week so we can lock terms into the June pilot order.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | markus.klein@redwood.com

Markus — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redline. I reviewed with Tom and our procurement lead; a few quick notes: 

1) Notice window: our standard practice is 45 days (not 60). For enterprise customers we sometimes accept 60, but for this pilot we need the ability to terminate with 45 days notice. Can we make the pilot-specific 45-day box the default for the Pilot Order Form?

2) TFC and transition: the paid 90-day transition option is reasonable, but procurement will need a clearer definition of \"pro-rata rate\" (monthly or daily), plus a cap on total transitional fees.

3) Procurement questionnaire: attaching our standard procurement_questionnaire_Orbyx.pdf — we need answers on data handling, support SLAs during the transition period, and any limitation on export of customer data during the notice phase.

Tom, looping you to confirm whether your legal team wants to review the redline or if you prefer us to send your counters directly to Markus.

Onward —
Elena
VP Product, Orbyx

Thanks Elena — appreciate the procurement questionnaire. I reviewed Markus's redline with a focus on commercial and operational risk; quick summary of suggested edits (attached as tracked changes in MSA_optout_safeguard_redline_v1.pdf):

- Notice window: propose default remain 60 days for standard Order Forms but allow the Pilot Order Form to elect 45 days explicitly via a checkbox and add a sentence that the pilot election is irreversible after signature to prevent downstream disputes.
- Definition clarity: replace \"pro-rata rate\" with \"pro-rata monthly fee based on remaining prepaid months at time of notice\"; add an example calculation in the Order Form amendment.
- Transition cap: add a maximum transitional fee equal to the unused pre-paid subscription balance (so no incremental penalty beyond remaining prepaid amounts).
- Abuse guardrail: limit unilateral TFC to one exercise per customer per 24-month rolling period; mutual TFC may be exercised without cap.
- SLA / data handling during notice: add a short clause guaranteeing customer can export data within 30 days of notice; Redwood will provide reasonable assistance (staffing-levels subject to the elected transition package).

Operational ask: Laura — can your team confirm that a 30-day export window (with reasonable assistance) is operationally feasible for pilot customers? If yes we'll add the language and circulate a final redline to Orbyx legal (copied: Will Harris) for review.

I also attached a lightweight OrderForm_amendment_draft.docx with the pilot checkbox and the sample calculation.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
